narrations: Welcome to Episode 3 of Hello World, pg_bio! If every cell in your body has the exact same DNA database, why is a brain cell different from a liver cell? The answer is Transcriptomics and allosteric regulation—which genes are turned on, and how distant residues talk to each other.

When scientists run Single-Cell RNA sequencing on 1 million cells across 20,000 human genes, it creates a 20-billion-point matrix. Because a cell only expresses about 2,000 genes at a time, over 90 percent of that matrix is zeroes. Storing dense columns in SQL or Pandas wastes gigabytes of RAM.
Systems engineers already know the cure: Compressed Sparse Row, or C-S-R. pg_bio implements a native SparseAttentionMap type using row pointers, column indices, and non-zero values.

Whether you are unpacking single-cell RNA dosage, traversing ESM-2 transformer attention heads with get_top_interacting_residues, or discovering cryptic allosteric pockets across 500-nanosecond molecular dynamics trajectories, CSR scans only the non-zero edges in microseconds.
That slashes memory by 90 percent and runs 31 times faster than dense Python matrices. Read the full deep dive at ideia dot me and explore pg_bio on GitHub.
